Day 1 of the third Ashes Test has thus far provided us with plenty of entertainment and with still plenty of time left in the final session, Australia will look to replicate England's effort with the ball. As the light starts to fade, Australia's pace battery will look to give it their all. It will be interesting to see how England's openers go about their business. Join us in a few minutes' time for the second innings.

Well, that was quick! What a comeback from Mark Wood and England! Australia went into the Tea break having lost the crucial wicket of Mitchell Marsh but still had solid batters to come. However, in a remarkable slump, they went from 240-5 to 263 all-out as Mark Wood ripped through the tail. Chris Woakes was the one to get the crucial wicket of Travis Head and that set everything in motion for England. From there on, the hosts kept on the pressure and didn't allow an inch to the Australian lower order. Wood finished off the innings with a stellar five-wicket haul.

England have let it slip big time in the post-Lunch session and will have to revisit their plans in the Tea break. They did create opportunities early in the session but a couple of spilled catches cost them dearly. The short ball ploy didn't bear fruit either and Ollie Robinson too hobbled off the pitch, leaving them a bowler short. The spin of Moeen Ali hasn't worked much either and they have leaked quite a few boundaries in this session. However, in the final over before Tea, Chris Woakes got rid of the big fish Mitchell Marsh and has allowed the hosts a big chance of coming back into the game. A crucial session awaits as both sides look to edge out the other at the end of Day 1. Join us for the final session in about 20 minutes' time.

SESSION SUMMARY - 26.1 overs, 149 runs and one wicket. What a turnaround this has been! Australia were reeling at 91/4 at the end of the first session but the pair of Travis Head and Mitchell Marsh has put on a monumental stand to not just get them back but slightly ahead in the game as well. Head was yet again peppered with short balls but managed to ride the storm and both batters did get a life or two as well. Marsh on the other hand looked positive right from the start and put away every single loose ball to bring up a sensational hundred. He did fall on the brink of Tea and Australia will now have to rebuild a bit after the break.

OUT! TAKEN! Chris Woakes gets the huge breakthrough! A huge sigh of relief for the England players as they see they finally see the back of Mitchell Marsh. Woakes bowls this on a good length and around off, Mitchell Marsh looks to have a poke at it but gets an inside edge onto his thigh pads as the ball loops up towards second slip where Zak Crawley takes an easy catch. There is a huge appeal for the catch, and Marsh starts walking back. He falls after an excellent hundred and Australia lose half their side now. THAT WILL BE TEA ON DAY 1.

A captivating session of Test cricket! England got off to a dream start as Stuart Broad got rid of David Warner in the very first over and for the 16th time in his career. Usman Khawaja and Marnus Labuschagne steadied things for the visitors for a bit. However, it was the fiery spell from Mark Wood that caught the attention of everyone as he was bowling really quick and removed Khawaja with a peach as well. After that, Chris Woakes followed it up by dismissing Labuschagne as the hosts got on top. Jonny Bairstow did drop both Travis Head and Steven Smith which could have proved more costly but Broad came back late in the session to send Smith back in the hut on his 100th Test. Mitchell Marsh and Head somehow managed to see the rest of the session out. England are all over Australia at the moment and will look to put more pressure post Lunch while the visitors need someone to bring a bit of calmness into their batting. Join us at 6.10 pm IST (12.40 pm GMT) to see how things pan out in the second session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 91 runs and 4 wickets in 26 overs. We saw some great pace bowling in this first session, especially from Mark Wood who was on fire. The hosts missed this kind of aggression in the first two Tests but will be glad to have him now as he has troubled the Aussies so far. The batters scored runs at a good rate as well o this quick outfield but England will be the happier side going into the break.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowling change. Wow, what a start to the Test match! Stuart Broad rocked Australia early by getting David Warner out but after that, Usman Khawaja and Marnus Labuschagne did well to ride the storm and steady the ship. The inclusion of Mark Wood has certainly made a difference as after a few extras, he has uprooted Khawaja and England are right on top of the proceedings here. Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match proceedings and it is now time for the 3rd Ashes Test to get underway. The two umpires are out in the middle as the players of England are seen in a huddle with the crowd cheering them on. Out comes the Australian opening pair of David Warner and Usman Khawaja who aren't greeted with a warm welcome at all. It will be Stuart Broad to have first bite at the red cherry and he is raring to go. Let's play...

Just five minutes away now from the start but first, the two sets of players will line-up for their respective national anthems. It will be Australia's national anthem first, followed by the national anthem of England.

Pat Cummins, the captain of Australia says that they would have bowled first as well but happy to bat as well. Adds that they will miss Lyon but Murphy has done well, especially in India and they back him. Mentions that it is an amazing achievement for Smith as he is playing his 100th Test and the standards that he has set is incredible. Informs there are three changes in the team, Cameron Green has a slight injury and Mitchell Marsh comes in for him, Scott Boland replaces Josh Hazlewood and Murphy in for Lyon.

Ben Stokes, the skipper of England says that they will have a bowl first and would be happy going either way, to be honest. Adds that with the injury to Pope, there were a few thought processes and they are happy with the team. Mentions that Harry Brook has played at number 3 in recent times but he can play anywhere as well. Says that the medical staff and Moeen Ali are confident that he can bowl and that he is a match-winner. Ends by saying that the support from the crowd has been phenomenal and the support here in Yorkshire will be brilliant as well with two Yorkshire boys in the line-up.

Australia (Playing XI) - David Warner, Usman Khawaja, Marnus Labuschagne, Steven Smith, Travis Head, Mitchell Marsh (In place of Cameron Green), Alex Carey (WK), Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins (C), Scott Boland (In for Josh Hazlewood), Todd Murphy (In place of Nathan Lyon).

England (Playing XI) - Zak Crawley, Ben Duckett, Harry Brook, Joe Root, Jonny Bairstow (WK), Ben Stokes (C), Moeen Ali (In place of Ollie Pope), Chris Woakes (In place of James Anderson), Mark Wood (In place of Josh Tongue), Ollie Robinson, Stuart Broad.
TOSS - Ben Stokes calls it right and England have elected to BOWL first.

Australia will be pretty content with how this series has panned out so far but they will be aware of the fact that this is the ground where four years earlier, Ben Stokes snatched the game out of their hands in one of the most remarkable Ashes innings ever. The absence of Nathan Lyon will certainly hurt a lot and Todd Murphy will have to bowl out of his skin to match Lyon's standards. The pace attack has been solid but there might be a change there as well and probably the only thing of concern is the form of Marnus Labuschagne who hasn't been near his best in recent times. Can Australia seal the series with two games to spare? Or will England come roaring back and add to the drama? We shall find out in due course. The all-important toss and team news in a bit.

England come into this Test with a huge amount of pressure on their shoulders as their coveted 'Bazball' has fallen short of what their opponents have had to offer. There have been a lot of positives and a return to form with the bat for Ben Stokes will be a bright light for them. The pace battery has been a concern with James Anderson out of touch and in all likeliness Chris Woakes and Mark Wood will get a go and Moeen Ali will come back in for the injured Ollie Pope. They will certainly need a big, big performance to upstage the in-form Aussies.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of Day 1 of the 3rd Ashes Test 2023 between England and Australia from Headingley in Leeds. If the drama leading to the series wasn't enough, the first two matches have provided us with plenty of blockbuster moments, none so bigger than the run-out of Jonny Bairstow in the previous game. Both matches have also gone down to the wire but the visitors have edged both of them and are on the brink of a remarkable away series win, their first Ashes series win since 2001. The hosts though will take inspiration from their talismanic skipper, Ben Stokes and look to cut Australia's lead in half.
